Class CreatedSlots

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.slot.CreatedSlots
public final class CreatedSlots extends Object
Adds real, server-synced, persistent slots to a vanilla menu. This is the library's half of slots a consumer composes itself, such as pockets or extra equipment slots.

Who calls this

The consumer calls CreatedSlots from their own mixin, injected at TAIL on the vanilla menu's constructor (InventoryMenu.<init>, for example). This path ships no such mixin and no slot registry, because owning a vanilla injection point or a hook consumers register into would make the library a platform. This class is a stateless helper the consumer's mixin calls directly; it registers and applies nothing on its own.

The vanilla constructor runs again every time the menu is rebuilt (login, respawn, dimension change, on both sides), so registering from there brings the slots back each time, with no separate lifecycle hook.

What you get

The slots are CreatedSlots over a standalone MenuPanel and SlotGroup, neither of which needs a CustomContainerMenu. That gives the usual inertness rules: when the panel is hidden the slots are invisible and inert, getItem returns EMPTY, they refuse placement and pickup, and vanilla skips them for rendering and hover. The reveal predicate below shows and hides the whole group at runtime.

Reveal on hover, and which side sees what

revealWhen(BooleanSupplier) drives the panel's visibility from a client-side predicate ("is the matching hotbar slot hovered", say). The helper applies it per side. On the server the panel is always visible, so getItem returns the real content and vanilla's broadcastChanges keeps syncing it. On the client the predicate controls rendering and input. That is why content survives while the panel is hidden: hiding is a client rendering choice, not server state. The predicate must be client-safe. It only ever runs on the client, but it should live in a client-only class so a dedicated server never loads client types.

Persistence and slot state

Item content persists when the slot is backed by a player- or block-attached Storage (see StorageAttachment), and vanilla's slot protocol syncs it at no extra cost. For per-slot state (lock flags and the like), back the slot with a KeyedStorage that returns a stable PersistentContainerKey; the SlotStateChannel API then works on these slots.

Creative and survival

The slots round-trip in both game modes with no consumer code. Survival edits reach the slot through vanilla's container-click path. A creative edit that vanilla's handleSetCreativeModeSlot would silently discard (the index is past vanilla's [1,45] range) is routed to the slot's backing Storage by the library's CreativeSetSlotMixin. Direct click-to-place works in both modes, and per-slot state comes along with it.

One menu only (use ContainerPanel for parity)

onto adds slots to the one menu the consumer's mixin targets (such as InventoryMenu). It does not project onto other menus: open a chest and the slots are not there. That is on purpose, since onto is the narrow tool for one menu whose mixin the consumer owns. For container parity (the same slots on every container screen, with the foreign-menu projection and creative wiring, from one call and no mixin) use ContainerPanel.define(String). It builds on this and adds the projection and the panel around the slots. Use onto only when you want slots on one menu you mix into.

Known limitation

Shift-click into these slots does not work by default, because vanilla's quickMoveStack knows nothing about them. Direct click-to-place works in both modes. Full shift-click routing is up to the consumer (who may override quickMoveStack in their own mixin), or left for later.

Recipe

// Mod init, declare the persistent storage once:
public static final PlayerStorageAttachment<NonNullList<ItemStack>> POCKETS =
    StorageAttachment.playerAttached("inventory-plus", "pockets", 3);

// Consumer mixin, @Inject(method = "<init>", at = @At("TAIL")) on InventoryMenu:
Storage storage = POCKETS.bind(player);              // or a KeyedStorage for metadata
CreatedSlots.RegisteredSlots pockets = CreatedSlots.onto((AbstractContainerMenu)(Object) this, player)
    .panel("inventory-plus:pockets")
    .group("pockets")
    .category(SlotGroupCategory.PLAYER_INVENTORY)       // required: what the group is to other mods
    .storage(storage)
    .layout(originX, originY, 3)                      // screen-relative origin + columns
    .revealWhen(() -> PocketHoverState.isRevealed())  // client-side predicate
    .register();

// Client init (ONCE, NOT per menu construction), wire the PRESENTATION half.
// register() above added the synced slot data; this draws the slots:
ClientSlots.renderGroup("inventory-plus:pockets", "pockets", 3, 3,
        OutsideRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP, ScreenPanelAdapter.DEFAULT_PADDING,
        ScreenMatcher.all());
